verdict.rationale: Decagon documents multiple surfaces where natural language substitutes for code/UI configuration: Agent Operating Procedures let teams 'define agent behavior in natural language' instead of SDKs (decagon-docs-16, decagon-docs-36), Watchtower lets users 'define what matters using natural language' for flagging criteria (decagon-docs-8, decagon-docs-20), and Ask AI enables 'flexible, conversational queries' for analytics (decagon-docs-9, decagon-docs-30). This shows broad NL-driven operation across agent-building, monitoring, and reporting, but all evidence is first-party marketing copy with no independent or hands-on corroboration, and full product administration (integrations, deployment, security settings) still appears UI/console-driven rather than command-driven. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on verification of natural-language operation, evidence that core admin/config tasks beyond AOP/Watchtower/Insights can be driven purely by NL commands.
